close_reason: Closed in single doc pass commit. The new '# Contract guarantees' (or '# Features') section in pkix-truststore/src/lib.rs covers this finding.
description:
pkix-truststore/Cargo.toml:21 declares an optional `serde` feature. When
enabled it adds `serde::Serialize + serde::Deserialize` derives to
`Error` (lib.rs:213-216) and `IoFailure` (lib.rs:104-107), and
propagates via `pkix-path/serde` so the re-exported `DerError`
participates in the same wire form.

The rustdoc on the public API does NOT tell callers this feature
exists or what it gates:

- The crate-level `# Stability` section (lib.rs:55-58) mentions only
  `#[non_exhaustive]` on `Error`. No mention of serde.
- The `Error` struct docs (lib.rs:200-212) discuss cache-friendliness
  but say nothing about `Serialize`/`Deserialize` requiring a feature.
- The `IoFailure` struct docs (lib.rs:99-103) mention "gaining
  `Clone`, `Eq`, and `Serialize`" but do not state that `Serialize`
  requires the `serde` feature flag. To a fresh caller this reads as
  "always serializable."
- No `# Features` section anywhere.

The per-section prompt template (api-contract,versioning) says:
> Cargo features added that change public types or method signatures
> conditionally — the API surface depends on the feature set in ways
> callers may not realize.

This is exactly that.

What goes wrong for a caller in production:

1. They write `let bytes = serde_json::to_vec(&err)?;` against
   `pkix_truststore::Error`, get `Error: !Serialize`, check docs.rs,
   find nothing about serde, eventually figure it out by reading
   source or Cargo.toml.

2. A cross-process cache pattern (the exact use case AGENTS.md
   non-negotiable #6 calls out): producer side builds with default
   features (no serde), consumer side builds with `features = ["serde"]`.
   They blame the cache library before realizing the dependency-graph
   feature unification rules played a role.

3. A Tier 2 sibling crate (`pkix-truststore-system`,
   `pkix-truststore-pkcs11`) wants to re-export `pkix_truststore::Error`
   and conditionally forward the serde behavior; without docs on what
   the feature does, the sibling crate author must read source.

Cargo.toml:39-40 sets `package.metadata.docs.rs.all-features = true`,
so docs.rs WILL render the serde-gated impls — but rendering implies
"always available" rather than "behind a feature gate." The
conventional rustdoc pattern attaches `#[cfg_attr(docsrs,
doc(cfg(feature = "serde")))]` to the impls so the gate is visible in
generated docs; the `#![cfg_attr(docsrs, feature(doc_cfg))]` at
lib.rs:1 already enables this nightly attribute but no `doc(cfg(...))`
annotations actually use it.

Fix (small, additive):

Add a `# Features` section to the crate-level rustdoc:

```
//! # Features
//!
//! `serde` (off by default) — derive `serde::Serialize` and
//! `serde::Deserialize` for [`Error`] and [`IoFailure`] so trust-store
//! load failures can be cached or sent across process boundaries
//! (AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6).
```

And add `#[cfg_attr(docsrs, doc(cfg(feature = "serde")))]` to the
`io_error_kind_serde` module + the gated derive lines so docs.rs
renders a visible "Available on crate feature serde only" badge.
title: API surface depends on serde feature but rustdoc never mentions the feature exists
